st.headline: Not SGX’s fault if stocks have no liquidity, says chairman: Markets this week
st.teaser: From Oct 5, SGX will reduce the standard board lot size from 100 units to 10 units for 11 companies.
fullText: SINGAPORE – Listed companies should proactively disclose their three- to five-year strategies so that investors can better understand their businesses and growth prospects, with board chairs leading the effort, Singapore Exchange chairman Koh Boon Hwee said on Oct 1.
He was speaking at an event organised by the Singapore Institute of Directors .
Koh said Singapore has strongly signalled its desire to reform its stock market, and more capital is already starting to flow in.
However, small and medium-sized enterprises cannot solely depend on the SGX to boost their valuations, as the bourse does not create liquidity nor demand and supply.

He said: “If you say that the market misunderstands you, it is your job to make sure that it understands you. If you say that there is no liquidity, it is because you have not been talking to the people who might have an interest in buying or demanding the stock.”
Therefore, it is incumbent upon companies and their leaders to communicate their growth strategies to the public.
“The exchange can’t do that for you, neither can it guarantee that your counter will be liquid.”
Koh said privatisation could be an option for companies whose shares are thinly traded and which are reluctant to disclose their long-term plans publicly.
His comments echoed a point made in his annual letter to shareholders on Sept 29, in which he said that “privatisation is not a tragedy but a rational and often healthy outcome”.
“For a listed company with limited growth prospects, low trading liquidity and persistently low valuations, going private is a sensible path,” he wrote.
“It serves little purpose for a company to remain listed simply so that an exchange can preserve its company count.”
Shares of City Developments Limited (CDL) fell by more than 14% through the week, after the property giant announced a three-year road map on Sept 28 .

The counter fell 5.7% by midday after its plans were unveiled before the market opened, and later closed 8.1% down at $7.59. It continued to slide and closed the week at $7.04, the lowest since Nov 2025.

Explaining why CDL’s share price fell, analysts said weak market conditions and the interest rate outlook could make it difficult for CDL to divest $6 billion worth of assets as planned. Details on where CDL intends to invest an additional $5 billion are also lacking.

In addition, doubts remain over whether the feud between chief executive Sherman Kwek and his father, executive chairman Kwek Leng Beng, has truly subsided. In early 2025, the father accused his son of orchestrating a boardroom takeover.
The elder Kwek was also absent from the Sept 28 unveiling of the road map, which left questions on succession from the media unanswered.
Others noted that some institutional investors have been dumping CDL shares in a typical “buy the rumour, sell the news” fashion, while some have also been short selling the shares.
CDL had said on Sept 28 that it plans to sell $6 billion worth of non-core assets, including $1.8 billion worth of hotels, over the next three years.

The company will also deploy $5 billion of growth capital, with Singapore remaining the principal market for new investments. A third of the funds has been earmarked for investments in China, where the property market has been weak, and Japan.

In addition, CDL plans to achieve a dividend payout of more than 35% annually, increase its assets under management from $5 billion to $10 billion, and lock in more than $1 billion in profit after tax and minority interests to be realised from divestment gains, over the three years.
DFI Retail Group’s shares jumped 6.6% when the market opened on Oct 1 and closed at US$3.41, the week’s peak, before falling the following day to close the week 6.1% lower at US$3.10.
The company said on Sept 1 that it will take full control of Starbucks’ licensed operations in the region , including Singapore, from Maxim’s Caterers, following a reorganisation.

Currently, DFI and Hongkong Caterers each own a 50% stake in Maxim’s Caterers. The new arrangement will see Hongkong Caterers retain Maxim’s other food and beverage businesses, which include five brands in Singapore: Genki Sushi, sen-ryo, Yakiniku Like, Butahage and Uoharu.

The reorganisation is slated to be completed by end-March 2027 and expected to immediately boost DFI’s revenue and profitability. DFI will transfer its 50% stake in Maxim’s to Hongkong Caterers for US$340 million (S$434.7 million) in cash, which it intends to deploy for growth or return to its shareholders as special dividends.

The group plans to build on the coffee chain’s leading position in Asia’s breakfast market by expanding its food and beverage menus and attracting more customers at lunchtime and later in the day, said Andrew Wong, chief executive of DFI IKEA, who will oversee the Starbucks operations.
DFI also plans to broaden Starbucks’ breakfast and bakery offerings, and adapt menus to local tastes.

More outlets are expected to open across Singapore as well as Thailand, Hong Kong, Macau, Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos between 2027 and 2029, taking the total number of Starbucks outlets in Asia to 1,350 from 1,110 currently. The Starbucks business in the seven Asian markets generated US$746 million in revenue in 2025.

The reorganisation comes at a time when competition for the coffee and tea consumer in Asia is intensifying. Chinese coffee giant Luckin Coffee already runs 103 outlets in Singapore – just three years after it first opened in the Republic.
Two companies have lodged their preliminary prospectuses to list on SGX.

Metasurface Technologies, which specialises in precision machining and precision welding for international customers in the industrial sector, filed its prospectus for a dual primary listing on the Catalist board on Sept 28.

cna.headline: Marquez wins Japanese GP to cut Martin's lead
cna.teaser: Marquez wins Japanese GP to cut Martin's lead
fullText: MOTEGI, Japan, Oct 4 : Ducati's Marc Marquez won his fourth Japanese Grand Prix to complete a sprint-race double at the Motegi Circuit on Sunday and cut title rival Jorge Martin's championship lead to two points.
Polesitter Martin managed to hold on to his advantage off the line and appeared comfortable in the opening eight laps as Marquez waited for the perfect moment to pounce.
That opportunity came on the 11th lap when Martin left a sliver of space on his inside, which Marquez exploited to take the lead.
The reigning champion then controlled the race to the chequered flag, finishing ahead of Aprilia's Martin and Marco Bezzecchi.
A single handpicked story that we think you shouldn't miss. Just one a day.

listening.title: The Green Transition of Singapore's Public Buses
listening.transcript: Singapore's Land Transport Authority is accelerating its transition to a fully electric bus fleet by 2040. Under this initiative, older diesel buses are systematically being decommissioned to slash vehicular emissions. Commuters can expect quieter rides and cleaner air as these eco-friendly alternatives are rolled out islandwide.

economistArticle.title: Research on grasping bureaucrats startles Singapore
paras: A minor academic tremor has sent ripples through the usually placid waters of Singapore's public administration. The cause is a research paper examining "grasping" bureaucrats—those who leverage their administrative power to extract rents or personal gain. For a city-state that prides itself on maintaining a squeaky-clean, meritocratic civil service, even the academic discussion of such behavior within regional proximity causes significant discomfort.

The study, though intended as a broad regional analysis of how civil service structures across Southeast Asia manage systemic rent-seeking, accidentally struck a delicate nerve. Singapore's administrative model is globally renowned for its high remuneration packages, designed precisely to deter graft. Consequently, the mere insinuation that technocrats might engage in grasping practices—even in a comparative or theoretical academic context—challenged local exceptionalism.

Critics of the study argue that its methodology lacked the contextual nuance required to differentiate Singapore's highly disciplined technocracy from the systemic patronage found elsewhere. They assert that the civil service's performance is driven by key performance indicators, not personal accumulation. To lump Singaporean administrators into a generalized framework of regional opportunism is, in their eyes, analytically flawed and unfair.

Yet, the controversy is perhaps more revealing about Singapore's academic culture than the actual integrity of its civil service. Higher education institutions in Singapore, heavily state-funded yet fiercely ambitious to climb global rankings, exist in a perpetual state of friction. They must navigate the demanding expectations of international academic freedom while remaining sensitive to local political boundaries.

In the end, Singapore's civil service remains exemplarily clean, and its reputation is unlikely to be tarnished by a single scholarly paper. However, the episode highlights the persistent sensitivity surrounding the nation's public image. For local researchers, the lesson is clear: when examining the delicate machinery of state power, even the most abstract academic models can robustly shake the ground beneath them.
economistArticle.cn:
一场小小的学术风波，在通常平静的新加坡公共行政领域激起了涟漪。其起因是一篇研究“贪婪”官僚（即利用行政权力谋取租金或个人利益的官员）的学术论文。对于一个以维持廉洁、精英治理的公务员体系而自豪的城邦国家而言，即便是在区域范围内对这种行为进行学术探讨，也会引起显着的不适。

该研究虽然旨在对东南亚各地的公务员结构如何应对系统性寻租行为进行广泛的区域分析，但却无意中触碰到了敏感的神经。新加坡的行政模式因其高薪制而在全球享有盛誉，其设计初衷正是为了遏制贪腐。因此，即便是在比较或理论学术语境中，仅仅暗示技术官僚可能存在贪婪行径，也挑战了当地的“例外论”。

该研究的批评者认为，其方法论缺乏必要的背景细微差别，无法将新加坡高度纪律化的技术官僚体制与该地区其他地方存在的系统性分赃体制区分开来。他们断言，公务员的业绩是由关键绩效指标驱动的，而非个人财富积累。在他们看来，将新加坡的行政人员归入区域投机主义的泛化框架中，在分析上是有缺陷且不公平的。

然而，这场争议或许更能揭示新加坡的学术文化，而非其公务员体系的实际廉洁度。新加坡的高等教育机构虽然主要由政府资助，但又极具跻身全球排名的野心，它们一直处于一种微妙的摩擦状态中。它们既要应对国际学术自由的苛刻要求，又要对当地的政治界限保持敏感。

归根结底，新加坡的公务员队伍依然堪称廉洁典范，其名誉不太可能因一篇学术论文而受损。然而，这一事件凸显了围绕国家公共形象的持续敏感性。对于本地学者来说，教训显而易见：在审视国家权力的精密机制时，即使是最抽象的学术模型，也能强力地震动其立足之地。

gems.s: Yet, the controversy is perhaps more revealing about Singapore's academic culture than the actual integrity of its civil service.
gems.why: This sentence uses a comparative 'more revealing about A than B' structure to shift the reader's focus from the obvious topic (corruption) to a deeper, underlying issue (academic self-censorship). This is a classic analytical technique used to challenge conventional assumptions. 中文解释：该句使用了“更能揭示A而非B”的比较结构，将读者的注意力从显而易见的主题（腐败）转移到更深层的潜在问题（学术自我审查）。这是一种典型的用于挑战常规假设的分析性修辞手法。
